_comment: Hostnames of the VENDOR / index APIs the skill queries (never the investigated target). The egress pool exists to keep the analyst's IP away from the TARGET; a vendor API sees only a licensed key. When every exit in the pool refuses the CONNECT tunnel to one of these hosts (a per-destination block at the proxy provider — observed: every exit answers 'Tunnel connection failed: 500' for fofa.info while serving every other host), the FailoverOpener falls back to a DIRECT request for that host only, and the refusal is not charged against the exits' health (it is not the exit that is broken). Targets are never given this fallback: for them CTI_PROXY_ALLOW_DIRECT governs, and its default is off. Add a host here only if it is an API you hold credentials for. Archive/Wayback hosts are deliberately EXCLUDED: fetching an archived page reveals the analyst IP and the target URL to archive.org, which is what the pool protects on a hostile case — those never take the direct fallback.
